subject: Intermittent egress failures after Brightfield private cutover - SNAT port skew
messages:
From: James Park <james.park@brightfield.io>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Brightfield NOC <noc@brightfield.io>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent outbound failures since private cutover

Hi Mateo,

We cut over to the Redwood Private deployment in our us-west VPC last night. Since then some of our services intermittently fail to reach external APIs (500+ SYN retries observed). The failures appear to affect a subset of flows only — roughly 10-15% of client sessions every 10-20 minutes.

What we have captured:
- tcpdump attached (brightfield-tcpdump-20270402.pcap) showing repeated SYN -> no SYN-ACK -> SYN retry cycles for affected sessions
- No obvious firewall drops on our side; counters look clean
- We see many flows from different internal IPs get SNATed to the same ephemeral source port on your egress NAT boxes, then subsequent connections from the same backend fail until the ephemeral port rotates

Can you confirm whether there were any NAT config changes or asymmetric routing introduced in the cutover? Will share more traces if useful. This is impacting live traffic.

Thanks,
James Park
Network Engineer, Brightfield Labs

Initial read: your note about multiple internal IPs mapping to the same ephemeral source port is suspicious — could be SNAT port preservation / port pooling behavior or a hashing skew across the SNAT fleet.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi to pull NAT translation table snapshots and egress hashing config (we'll attach).
2) Laura and I will check if any new routing policies or ECMP changes were applied during the cutover.
3) Temporary mitigation: expand ephemeral port range + enable per-connection port allocation on affected boxes to avoid port reuse collisions.

— Mateo

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Intermittent outbound failures since private cutover

Looping in details from the NAT boxes. I pulled the translation table and egress SNAT config; attached snippet (egress-nat-table.txt). Observations:
- We are running a sticky SNAT implementation that attempts to preserve source ports for session affinity when possible.
- During last night's deployment we rolled a scale set change that altered the per-node hashing seed; that can cause a short window where new flows land on different SNAT nodes and port collisions occur if ephemeral port reuse is high.
- Ephemeral port range defaults are narrow: 32768-61000. Under your workload bursts, reuse probability spikes.

Short-term mitigation I recommend:
- Increase ephemeral port range on the SNAT boxes to 20000-65535 (reduces collision probability).
- Force per-connection port allocation for 30m on the affected node group to avoid port reuse.
- Add a temporary NAT overflow bucket to accept additional translations if the primary table fills.

I can push a safe, reversible change within the hour if you approve a 15-minute brief maintenance window with rolling restarts of the SNAT agents.

— Rishi
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick runbook and change notes for the window:
- Pre-checks (10m): capture conntrack counts, NAT table occupancy, current ephemeral range, ECMP next-hop distribution.
- Change (5-10m): expand ephemeral range to 20000-65535, enable per-connection port allocation flag on SNAT daemons, toggle overflow bucket. No config reload needed for hashing seed change; SNAT agent rolling restart will pick new seed.
- Post-checks (10m): compare NAT collisions/port-reuse metrics, validate tcpdump success on sample flows, verify no SG (security group) rejects were introduced.
- Rollback plan: restore ephemeral range and disable per-connection flag, revert overflow bucket; rolling restart back to previous agents.

I've attached the proposed script (proposed-snat-fix.sh) and the private egress runbook reference (runbook-private-egress.md). I'll run the change at 18:05 PDT and report status.

— Laura
Principal Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

We ran validation post-change for ~8 hours. Results:
- No new SYN retries observed in the sampled traces; previously affected flows now complete the 3-way handshake reliably.
- NAT table occupancy is stable; collision counters dropped to baseline.
- No security group rejects observed on our side.

Thanks for the quick triage and clean rollback plan. Two action items for follow-up:
1) Can Redwood add automated nat-collision alerts to the private console (threshold slack + runbook link)?
2) Let's schedule a post-mortem to capture the root cause: interaction between hashing seed roll and ephemeral range under bursty pod churn.

We're marking the incident resolved for now. Will open BF-4789 in your Jira for the post-mortem notes.

— James Park
